name: Marsha Blackburn
bio: Tennessee's senior U.S. senator since 2019, Blackburn is the polling frontrunner with broad establishment support and statewide name recognition. Trump-aligned conservative.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Blackburn has no specific pre-K or early childhood education proposal in her governor campaign. She continues to emphasize school choice and parental rights, supporting the Education Freedom Scholarship and public charter school expansion. Her May 2026 polling-dominating campaign focuses on education broadly but not early childhood investment.
early_childhood_ed.details: Blackburn's Senate education page emphasizes that parents — not government — should have the final say in schooling choices regardless of zip code or socioeconomic status. She introduced the Educational Choice for Children Act to fund K–12 scholarship awards at the federal level. In a May 2026 Nashville Banner article highlighting her 56-point polling lead, her campaign focus on the voucher/school choice issue was confirmed, with no mention of pre-K or childcare expansion. She expressed support for public charter schools expanding to suburban and rural areas in a Tennessee Firefly interview. A 2026 TQEE report documenting that 60% of Tennessee third-graders are behind has not produced a specific Blackburn response. Her silence on pre-K investment is consistent with her historical opposition to universal preschool as a federal spending priority.

child_hunger.summary: Blackburn voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill in July 2025, which cuts SNAP by approximately $187 billion over 10 years and shifts administrative costs to states — despite her earlier co-sponsorship of the Keep SNAP Funded Act in October 2025. She has publicly framed the SNAP changes as eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse. Her governor campaign has not addressed Tennessee's child hunger crisis; the Tennessee legislature allocated $7 million in April 2026 to fund Summer EBT beginning in 2027, unlocking an estimated $90 million in federal dollars for 700,000 children, but Blackburn issued no statement on this development.
child_hunger.details: In her Senate statement on the One Big Beautiful Bill, Blackburn said the legislation 'prevents the largest tax hike in American history' and would make SNAP 'stronger and healthier.' In a statement to Fox13, she said the bill is 'rooting out waste, fraud and abuse' and removing access for 'fraudsters, freeloaders and illegal immigrants.' She did not address the approximately 700,000 Tennessee children who qualify for Summer EBT but will not receive it in summer 2026 — the legislature's April 2026 $7 million allocation only restores the program for 2027, unlocking an estimated $90 million in federal dollars. Safety net advocates had urged her to vote no on the One Big Beautiful Bill, citing an estimated $110 million annually in new costs shifted to Tennessee taxpayers and risks to the state's 695,000+ SNAP recipients. The bill imposes new work requirements on adults aged 55–64 and parents of children 14 and older. Blackburn's rural health bills co-sponsored in March 2026 addressed hospital finances but did not address child nutrition.

parental_support.summary: Blackburn's signature parental support positions remain the Working Families Tax Cuts embedded in the One Big Beautiful Bill: a permanent, expanded Child Tax Credit ($2,200), enhanced employer childcare tax credit (expanded from $150,000 to $500,000), and a paid family and medical leave credit. Her 2026 governor campaign frames these as delivering an average $2,660 tax benefit to Tennessee families.
parental_support.details: Blackburn's Senate statement on the One Big Beautiful Bill highlighted the enhanced child tax credit made permanent as a key win for Tennessee families. The bill permanently expands the employer-provided childcare tax credit from $150,000 to $500,000, which Blackburn has cited as a family support tool. The Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act she co-sponsored was signed into law in 2026, streamlining pediatric Medicaid enrollment across state lines — a health access benefit for families with children who have complex medical needs. She has also championed the Kids Online Safety Act as a digital-age parental support measure. No new parental support proposals specific to her governor campaign were found beyond reiterating these federal-level accomplishments.

name: John Rose
bio: Four-term congressman from the Cumberland Plateau leaving his House seat to run. Farmer and small-business owner from Cookeville.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: Rose has no specific early childhood education or pre-K proposal. His education platform centers on school choice, appointing a Tennessee-certified education commissioner, and Career and Technical Education. No childcare or pre-K positions have been identified in his campaign materials or public statements.
early_childhood_ed.details: Rose's campaign website and a Cleveland Banner opinion column on his education vision focus exclusively on K–12 issues: school choice options (public, private, charter, homeschool), appointing an education commissioner with Tennessee teaching experience, and expanding CTE. His first campaign promise is hiring a commissioner with 'Tennessee teaching experience.' He supports parental choice in education and improving the Department of Children's Services. No statements on pre-K, Head Start, childcare subsidies, or early childhood investment were found across his website, campaign materials, or governor race profiles.

child_hunger.summary: Rose has made one specific statement on SNAP as a gubernatorial candidate: he supports scrutinizing how SNAP benefits are spent, expressing support for restrictions on sugary treats. No position on Summer EBT, the Tennessee child hunger gap, or SNAP cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill was found.
child_hunger.details: In a WJHL interview, Rose stated SNAP benefits 'are supposed to be used' for supplemental nutrition and not sugary treats, and said it is 'right to take a careful look at how the money is used' to ensure benefits serve people 'who are in need.' This aligns with the SNAP junk-food restriction approach also supported by Blackburn. Rose voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill as a U.S. Representative, which included $187 billion in SNAP cuts over 10 years. His campaign website and candidate profiles contain no specific positions on Tennessee's Summer EBT gap, the 700,000 children at risk of hunger, or food bank capacity. His references to 'children's services' remain generic.

parental_support.summary: Rose has no specific parental support or childcare platform beyond school choice and improving the Department of Children's Services. He received a 100% Family Research Council rating in February 2026 and pledged to make Tennessee 'a national leader' on making adoption accessible to families.
parental_support.details: Rose's parental rights emphasis focuses on educational choice — stating 'parents must have a seat at the table' and that parents know what is best for their children's education. He pledged to improve the Department of Children's Services and to make adoption more attainable for Tennessee families, calling it a gubernatorial priority. His FRC 100% rating reflects alignment with faith, family, and freedom positions. As with early childhood ed and child hunger, no specific childcare subsidy, paid leave, or parental financial support proposals have been identified in his campaign platform or public statements.

name: Monty Fritts
bio: East Tennessee state legislator running on a populist conservative platform. Lower profile statewide than Blackburn or Rose.
photo_credit: No headshot found at direct image URL; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Fritts has no early childhood education or childcare proposal. He voted against the Tennessee Department of Education's continuation in sunset hearings, the only lawmaker to do so, and his education platform is focused on opposing school vouchers as unconstitutional. No pre-K or childcare investment positions have been found.
early_childhood_ed.details: Fritts was the only lawmaker to oppose the Tennessee Department of Education's continuation during legislative sunset hearings. He opposes the Education Freedom Scholarship program, calling it fiscally irresponsible and unconstitutional, and pledges to 'end fiscally irresponsible, unconstitutional voucher programs.' His campaign slogan 'Liberty & Less Government' and limited-government platform make new public spending on early childhood education unlikely to be part of his platform. His education positions, per a WGNS Radio opinion piece, ground his vision in a return to traditional educational values and public school investment, but no specific early childhood proposals were found. He supports parental rights for homeschool and private school choice, but without public subsidy.

child_hunger.summary: No specific positions on child hunger, SNAP, or Summer EBT have been found for Fritts. His limited-government platform and opposition to new spending programs suggests opposition to SNAP expansion, though no direct statement has been identified.
child_hunger.details: Fritts's limited-government, anti-spending platform ('Liberty & Less Government') and his support for eliminating programs he deems unconstitutional or fiscally irresponsible suggest he would not support expanded SNAP benefits or Summer EBT participation. However, no direct public statements or votes on child hunger, SNAP, or food insecurity have been found in searches of his legislative record, campaign website, or candidate profiles. His legislative tracking page on PolicyEngage covers 2025–2026 but no nutrition-related bills were identified. He supports eliminating the grocery tax, which would provide some indirect food affordability relief.

parental_support.summary: Fritts gained national attention in January 2026 for calling for capital punishment for parents of transgender children and providers of gender-affirming care, framing the position as scripturally mandated. No constructive parental financial support or childcare proposals have been found in his platform.
parental_support.details: In January 2026, Fritts appeared on a Christian nationalist podcast and called for state-sanctioned execution of parents, guardians, and medical professionals connected to gender-affirming care for minors under 18, stating the position 'aligns with scripture.' This drew widespread national condemnation. Beyond this, his parental rights positions focus on educational choice without public subsidy and limited government interference in family decisions. His opposition to 'new spending programs' means no paid leave, childcare subsidy, or other parental support financial measures are included in his platform. He challenges Plyler v. Doe to deny public school enrollment to undocumented children, a position affecting families with mixed immigration status.

name: Lauren Pinkston
bio: Independent gubernatorial candidate. Former Lipscomb University professor with a detailed family-economic platform — only candidate proposing redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship funds to early childhood ed and employer on-site daycare.
photo_credit: Direct headshot URL not found; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Pinkston strongly supports redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship funds to expand early childhood education and supports state investment in employer on-site daycare. She frames childcare expansion as an economic strategy to enable dual-income households and relieve financial pressure on young families.
early_childhood_ed.details: Pinkston's campaign platform proposes redirecting EFS funds toward early childhood education and supporting businesses that offer on-site daycare through state investment. Her goal is to increase the number of affordable early childhood education opportunities for Tennessee families. She framed her approach on the Loyal Opposition podcast in March 2026. Her platform on pinkstonfortn.com confirms these positions as of mid-2026. Her childcare expansion framing emphasizes economic outcomes for working families rather than equity or developmental outcomes, distinguishing her approach from Green's.

child_hunger.summary: Pinkston opposes SNAP purchase restrictions on certain foods, arguing they harm local grocers and drive up food costs. She supports reinstating Summer EBT and connecting it to local Tennessee farmers, and would offer additional SNAP funds to families who participate in nutrition classes.
child_hunger.details: Pinkston's platform explicitly opposes restricting SNAP benefits from purchasing snacks or sodas, warning such rules 'harm local grocers and drive up food costs.' She supports reinstating Summer EBT and connecting it to local Tennessee farmers. She would offer additional SNAP funds to families who participate in nutrition and food preparation classes, framing it as an incentive rather than a restriction. She also supports exploring grocery tax removal to reduce household food costs. Her approach on benefit cliffs addresses the dynamic where modest income gains cause families to lose food assistance. The May 2026 Vanderbilt Child Health Poll showing 36% of Tennessee families food insecure provides relevant context for her positions.

parental_support.summary: Pinkston supports eliminating benefit cliffs at DHS to prevent families from losing assistance when income rises modestly, redirecting EFS funds to early childhood education and employer daycare, and protecting TennCare coverage for the 50% of Tennessee children insured through the program. She also supports IVF and contraceptive access and collective bargaining rights for workers.
parental_support.details: Pinkston's platform includes restructuring public assistance to eliminate benefit cliffs — situations where earning more causes families to lose benefits — calling this a key economic relief mechanism for working parents. She has warned that TennCare premium doublings under federal cuts would be 'a tragedy' for Tennessee's 50%-plus of children covered by the program and pledged to protect it. She supports IVF and contraceptive access as family planning rights, noting she is the aunt of two children born through assisted reproductive technology. She supports collective bargaining rights, noting union membership in Tennessee has grown over 50% since 2020, framing worker rights as family stability. Her Lebanon Democrat profile confirms she is positioning herself as the candidate for working-class Tennesseans seeking a third option outside partisan extremes.

name: Jerri Green
bio: Democratic primary frontrunner running a coalition campaign rooted in West Tennessee. Focused on healthcare, education, and rural-urban balance.
photo_credit: Green for Governor official campaign website

early_childhood_ed.summary: Green maintains the strongest early childhood education platform in the 2026 field. She calls for universal pre-K statewide, a dedicated childcare and early education fund with investments in afterschool and summer care for households under $75,000, and a Day One commitment to invest $50M in TANF funds to clear the childcare waitlist. A February 2026 WJHL interview confirmed she wants subsidies for families below the poverty line to access quality, affordable childcare while ensuring childcare workers receive living wages.
early_childhood_ed.details: Green's policy page and Day One Plan center early childhood as a first-order priority. Her $50M TANF childcare proposal is framed as eliminating the waitlist so no parent has to choose between a paycheck and their child. She successfully won funding to increase Pre-K classes in Memphis during her time on the City Council, providing a concrete track record. Her dedicated childcare and early education fund would cover afterschool and summer care programming, extending beyond traditional pre-K. A February 16, 2026 WJHL interview confirmed she wants subsidies for families below the poverty line and living wages for childcare workers. The Special Education Equity Fund proposal addresses children with disabilities as federal Trump Administration cuts reduce services. Green's early childhood platform is the most detailed of all six candidates.

child_hunger.summary: Green has pledged to budget state funds to cover SNAP and EBT gaps for Tennesseans cut by the One Big Beautiful Bill, directly citing that 1 in 5 Tennessee children go to bed hungry. She supports ending the grocery tax and has a prior record of urging Gov. Lee to suspend the grocery tax during a federal shutdown.
child_hunger.details: In her February 16, 2026 WJHL policy interview, Green stated she would 'budget to fund those in need of SNAP/EBT benefits who were affected by the Big Beautiful Bill,' directly linking her child hunger position to the federal cuts. She stated: '1 in 5 kids right now in the state of Tennessee goes to bed hungry; our governor and government won't step up, and we can change that.' As Memphis City Councilwoman, she sent a November 2025 letter to Gov. Lee urging a temporary suspension of the 4% grocery tax during a federal shutdown. Her Day One Plan includes using $50M in TANF funds for the childcare waitlist, which also addresses food security indirectly by enabling parents to work. The May 2026 Vanderbilt Child Health Poll showing 36% of Tennessee families food insecure and 30% nutrition insecure strengthens the context for her positions.

parental_support.summary: Green's parental support platform includes paid family and medical leave, the $50M TANF childcare waitlist elimination on Day One, free diapers and ending the diaper tax, gun lock distribution (2,000 in Shelby County), and using $10M in TANF funds to waive security deposits for over 100,000 families seeking housing. Her campaign brand 'One Tough Mother' centers her identity as a mother of three driving her family policy positions.
parental_support.details: Green's Day One Plan commits to two TANF-funded family support actions: $50M to eliminate the childcare waitlist and $10M to waive security deposits helping over 100,000 families secure stable housing. Her platform calls for paid family and medical leave and a real living wage as essential to family stability. She has distributed 2,000 free gun locks in Shelby County, crediting the effort with a reported 25% decrease in gun violence — framing it as child safety for parents. She advocates for expanded Medicaid to support rural Tennessee families and for erasing predatory medical debt for 100,000+ Tennesseans. In January 2026, Shelby County Mayor Lee Harris appointed her Interim Chief Public Defender, overseeing 22,000+ annual cases, giving her direct exposure to family court and parental support issues.

name: Dr. Carnita Atwater
bio: Memphis community advocate making her second gubernatorial run. Known for community development work in the New Chicago neighborhood.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific early childhood education or childcare positions have been found for Atwater. Her campaign focuses on equity, community advocacy, and broad educational access, but no pre-K, childcare subsidy, or early learning investment proposals are articulated in her campaign materials.
early_childhood_ed.details: Atwater's About Me page describes 30-plus years of service to children, senior citizens, single parents, and displaced populations across Tennessee, establishing her as a community practitioner rather than a policy-platform candidate. A justmymemphis.com profile confirmed she supports workforce training and youth empowerment broadly but contains no specific early childhood education proposals. Her campaign website returned a 404 error, limiting access to any updated platform. A Ballotpedia survey response on 'portable food satellites in every food desert' shows her policy communication style — community-service framing rather than legislative proposal framing. She has not responded to the 2026 TQEE early childhood policy brief or the Vanderbilt data showing 60% of Tennessee third-graders behind.

child_hunger.summary: Atwater's Ballotpedia survey response proposes 'portable food satellites in every food desert' as her primary food security initiative. A justmymemphis.com profile notes she pledges to 'release withheld funds for food assistance' and prioritize low-income families in state budgets. No SNAP-specific positions or Summer EBT statements were found.
child_hunger.details: Atwater's most specific food policy proposal remains the 'portable food satellites in every food desert' from her Ballotpedia survey — a community-service model consistent with her founding of food programs for elderly Memphis residents. A justmymemphis.com profile found she pledges to 'release withheld funds for food assistance' and frames budgets as 'moral documents' with spending priorities shifted toward vulnerable populations, but without SNAP-specific details. No statements on the One Big Beautiful Bill SNAP cuts, the Summer EBT gap affecting 700,000 Tennessee children in summer 2026, or the Vanderbilt May 2026 polling on food insecurity were found. Her poverty reduction and community advocacy framing implies support for food assistance but without the specificity of Pinkston's or Green's positions.

parental_support.summary: Atwater has no specific parental support policy proposals — no paid leave, childcare subsidy, or family financial support programs are articulated. Her campaign draws on her personal history of fostering 92 children and 30-plus years of community service as evidence of commitment to families and children, but this has not translated into specific platform proposals.
parental_support.details: Atwater's most distinctive family credential is her personal history of fostering 92 children from diverse backgrounds, which she says gives her unique rapport with young people and deep understanding of low-income family challenges. Her campaign materials describe decades of direct service — feeding, clothing, sheltering, and advocating for families — but do not translate into specific gubernatorial policy proposals on parental leave, childcare, or family financial support. She has sheltered over 100 domestic violence victims in private locations, showing direct parental safety engagement, but no formal shelter or support program proposals emerged in her governor campaign. The campaign website errors persist, limiting access to any updated platform. She remains a long shot in the Democratic primary against Green.
